title: Machine-learning inverse design of nanofiltration membranes for Mg2+/Na+ separation
summary: A workflow combining a curated 1,253-entry dataset, extremely randomized tree regressors (test-set R2 above 0.79) and Bayesian optimization with a scalarized objective produced inverse-designed thin-film composite membrane recipes. Two designed membranes were fabricated and measured, showing favorable Mg2+/Na+ selectivity. The date is that of the ChemRxiv v2 record, the abstract gives no quantitative selectivity or number of recipes tested, and the dataset mixes literature and in-house records.
ai_technology: Extremely randomized tree regressors for forward prediction with Bayesian optimization for inverse design of nanofiltration membranes

evidence.tested: Two inversely designed membrane recipes were fabricated and measured experimentally; a held-out test set evaluated forward prediction.
evidence.unknown: Quantitative selectivity values, number of recipes tested and earlier-version dates; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Tree-based regressors predicted membrane performance and Bayesian optimization proposed recipes.
